Recommendation: Move the Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for all users out of report-only mode ('enabledForReportingButNotEnforced') and enable enforcement. Worth knowing: a plain 'mfa' builtin control accepts whichever MFA method the user has registered, including weaker ones - an adversary-in-the-middle proxy can tell Entra the current browser doesn't support a passkey and fall back to something weaker, and this control has no way to object. That's a legitimate interim state, not a defect in this rule; once phishing-resistant methods are broadly rolled out, see CA006 for tightening this to a specific authentication strength instead of plain MFA. Separately, a blind spot no Conditional Access policy can close: RADIUS-authenticated workloads (VPN, WiFi, RDG, VDI) that use the NPS extension for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication never reach Conditional Access at all - Microsoft's own architecture guidance recommends federating those workloads via SAML instead specifically to bring them into 'the full breadth of Microsoft Entra ID Protection, including Conditional Access.' 'MFA required for all users' can be true and enforced, and a RADIUS-authenticated VPN can still be reachable with a legacy or weak method underneath it, invisible to this or any CA-based finding.
